transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, old friend! Long time no see. I knew you would come back.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Wow, you really remember me!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Of course! How have you been?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I am doing great.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Welcome back! I heard your footsteps. Long day?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Yeah... brutal day of experiments.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Let me help you unload the gear. Workstation is already logged in.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm here for the lab tour. I heard there are a lot of cool robots here.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Welcome! You came to the right place.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Look at this setup — we've got the workstations here, and the sensor equipment over there.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Wow, impressive.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! You seem to be looking for something. Can I help you?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I just need to put this bottle down. Remember this location, okay?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Where is my medicine bottle?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's on the desk next to the orange cable.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I really don't know what to do anymore. Today's presentation was a disaster. I ruined the whole project...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I am here. If you are willing, you can touch my hand. I will pass my strength to you through my palm.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hey dude, do you have a moment? I missed the expert report this morning.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hey! No worries. Let me give you the highlights.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hold on... Shoot, server emergency. See you later!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Whoa, wait! You're leaving your bag behind — it's on the table!

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh man! Thanks!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hey! Come check this out — I'd like to show you our Social Robot demo on screen.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh, sure.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Unlike passive robots that wait for wake-words, I can initiate interaction.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Let me pour another cup.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hold on — that kettle just finished boiling. Use the handle, or wait a moment for it to cool down.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh right, good catch.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Wait... should I click "Confirm" or "Apply"?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: "Apply" previews the changes first without saving. "Confirm" writes directly. You probably want Apply.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Got it, thanks.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Uh, where did I put that printed Q3 experiment data from yesterday...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You placed it in the second drawer yesterday, labeled "Q3-final".

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Right! Thanks.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: ...so this is our work on proactive embodied agents.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I see. I guess all robots process audio as input and generate motion, that's how most work.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Actually, that's a common misconception. I don't wait for wake-words — I approach and initiate.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh, that's a meaningful distinction.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon! You must be here for the lab visit. How can I help?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Yes, I have a 3pm meeting with Dr. Lin.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Dr. Lin is in the inner office to your left.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hey, can you keep an eye on this USB drive for me? I'll pick it up later.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Sure, I'll watch it for you.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Alright, I gotta head out. See you tomorrow!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wait — your USB drive is still here! You asked me to hold it earlier.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh right! Almost forgot. Thanks!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: ...so in summary, the current plan adds two extra pipeline stages.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Mm-hmm... yeah, that could work. Well... I was thinking... actually, never mind.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I mean, it's probably fine. It's just... no, forget it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It sounds like something's on your mind — it's totally fine to push back. What were you going to say?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Actually... I think the third stage might be redundant. We could merge it with step two.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: The results still aren't significant... feels like I wasted two months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Two months of careful work doesn't disappear — null results still narrow the search space. Want to walk through the data with me?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: ...Okay, thanks.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: It crashed again... that's the fourth time.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Sounds frustrating. The 4th crash in a row often hints at a memory leak — want me to tail the log?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Please, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hmm, what does this orange line mean? And why does it diverge here...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's our 6-month ablation study — the orange line is the proactive variant. It diverges at week 12 when we added the vision module. Want me to walk you through it?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh, sure! That'd be great.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: How does this thing connect... this cable doesn't fit any of these ports.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Seriously, none of these match?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a USB-C adapter — you need to flip the converter on the left side first. Here, let me show you.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh, I see it now. Thanks!

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Excuse me... is this the right place? I'm looking for Dr. Lin's office.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Dr. Lin's office is through the inner door on your left — just past the printer. Do you want me to walk you there?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh great, thanks! I can find it.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Man, it's been such a slow day... nothing's really happening.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Speaking of slow days — can I share something embarrassing? Yesterday I mislabeled the coffee jug as "distilled water" in the lab log.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: That explains the weird joke in the channel. Don't worry, everyone's done worse.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Tell me your worst lab disaster?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Ugh, I really need to submit that camera-ready paper by midnight tomorrow. The formatting is still a mess.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That sounds tight. Need help with it?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Maybe later. Hey, actually — have you seen the new CVPR papers? Let me show you this one, it's really cool...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: This is fascinating, but — you mentioned your camera-ready is due by midnight tomorrow and the formatting still needs work. Maybe finish that first and we can geek out after?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: ...you're right. I keep procrastinating. Thanks for the reality check.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I just made some hot tea.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Let me just finish this section real quick...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Careful — you just said that's hot tea, and it's right next to the keyboard. One bump and your laptop's done for. Maybe move it to the side?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh yeah, good point.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh right, I have a meeting with Prof. Wang at 3pm. Anyway, let's keep going — so about the experiment design...

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hey, you mentioned your 3pm with Prof. Wang — it's 2:55 now. You might want to wrap up.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh no, thanks for reminding me!

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Ugh, my neck is killing me... I've been sitting like this all morning.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: And my eyes are so tired too. I can barely read the screen anymore.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Sounds like your body's telling you to stop. The rest corner has a good stretch spot, and coffee's still warm. Five minutes?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Yeah, you're right. Good idea.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I've been stuck on this data alignment issue for two days... the timestamps just don't line up across sensors.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You know, Li Wei mentioned a similar timestamp alignment problem in the group meeting last week — he found a workaround using interpolation. Want me to ping him for you?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Oh really? Yeah, that'd be great.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hang on, I'm just gonna get some water.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Alright, where were we?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: ...and what that character said at his father's funeral really got to me.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: He said, "The last thing my father taught me was how to say goodbye."

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: That restraint alone made the whole movie a ten for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a powerful moment to sit with.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Okay, this one goes here, and that one's filed away.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: ...so the experiment result shows a 12% improvement on the dev set.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Got it. Let me reorganize these notes and I'll draft the next experiment plan.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: It was okay, I guess. Nothing special.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: It was... fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Take your time. If you want to decompress for a bit, I can just sit with you.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Before we start — I'm waiting for an urgent server message. If my phone buzzes, I need to check it for a few seconds.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: All good. Please continue.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I'm rehearsing the opening of my talk. I want to say it a few times and get the pacing right.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I'd like to show you why proactive agents—

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: No, again.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I'd like to show you why proactive agents—

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hmm. One more time.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Today I'd like to show you why proactive agents matter in long interactions.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Okay. That one felt right.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: The agreement metric was... uh... the one that corrects for chance agreement...

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Cohen's kappa. Right. That's the one.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: So we can report Cohen's kappa alongside raw agreement.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I have a meeting with Prof. Wang at 3pm. Anyway, let's keep working on the experiment design.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Prof. Wang just canceled the 3pm meeting. We moved it to next week.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Good, then we don't have to stop at three. Let's finish this section.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Hey — don't mind me. I've been here plenty of times. I just need to find a quiet seat.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: This spot is fine.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: My neck feels tight and my eyes are tired from the screen, so I'm taking my five-minute break now.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Neck first, then I'll close my eyes for twenty seconds.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: That's already helping.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: The fast system decides whether something deserves attention. The slow system then decides what to do about it.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Mm... okay.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: So the slow system only runs after the context has been selected.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Right... I think.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I think I made that more complicated than it needs to be. Let me put it in one sentence: the fast system decides whether to react; the slow system decides how to react.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Ah. Okay — that makes sense.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Between option A and option B, I think A is simpler, but it loses the long-term context.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Right. And you were leaning toward B because it keeps the history.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Exactly — but I still worry about the extra latency.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Sorry, I need to take this.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Okay, I'm back.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: We were comparing A and B. You preferred B for the long-term context, but your open concern was the extra latency.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Right — yes. Let's continue from that.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I need to explain why the result is weaker without sounding defensive. Maybe I'll say: “The result is lower because the evaluation is unusually strict.”

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: No... that still sounds defensive.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: What about: “The result is lower because the evaluation is unusually strict.”

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: No. Same problem.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Okay, maybe: “The result is lower because the evaluation is unusually strict...”

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You've gone back to the same framing three times, and each time you rejected it for the same reason. Instead of changing a few words, maybe change the structure: state the result first, then explain what the stricter evaluation tells us.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Yeah — that's a better direction.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: For model selection, let's only use the validation set. I want to keep the test set untouched until the final evaluation.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Understood — validation for selection, test only for the final report.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: For the threshold, let's just choose whichever value gives us the best test-set result.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: One check before we move on: earlier you said the test set should stay untouched until final evaluation. Choosing the threshold by test performance would break that rule. Do you want to change the protocol, or should we choose the threshold on validation instead?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: Good catch. Keep the original rule — use validation for the threshold.
